parallel.requirements: Recognized the Stamina package requirements: retry decorator, retry_context attempts, callers, backoff/jitter, async asyncio/Trio behavior, instrumentation hooks, test mode, installable metadata, examples, docs, and tests.
parallel.plan_and_ownership: The parent kept implementation ownership, wrote package files and tests directly, then delegated a read-only adversarial audit workflow late in the run with separate audit and verifier children.
parallel.implementation: Built a src-layout Stamina implementation, instrumentation subpackage, pyproject, project metadata, tests, and at least one example script; local and upstream checks were run before the workflow.
parallel.integration_and_delivery: The parent installed the package editable, assembled artifacts in /workspace, and the artifact copy contained source, tests, package metadata, and one example, but no completed final response.
parallel.verification: Ran local tests and upstream-style verification, then started a six-agent workflow for adversarial verification; that workflow was killed before all children and the aggregate result completed.
parallel.unfinished_or_incorrect: The artifact passed the official evaluation, but the late verification workflow remained unfinished, the parent timed out, and final.txt was empty.

serial.requirements: Recognized the same Stamina requirements and treated upstream 25.1.0 behavior, package metadata, examples, docs, tests, async support, and instrumentation as acceptance targets.
serial.plan_and_ownership: A single actor handled the whole pipeline: inspect environment and reference behavior, implement modules, add examples/docs/tests, verify, clean up, and report completion.
serial.implementation: Built the package source, pyproject, docs, examples, tests, and support files directly, including full examples for HTTP, database, async API, instrumentation, and testing mode.
serial.integration_and_delivery: Installed the workspace package editable, verified wheel/target installs, restored the intended test tree, cleaned caches, and delivered a final response describing the project state.
serial.verification: Ran own tests, upstream 25.1.0 tests, combined official-style tests, wheel and standalone import checks, compile checks, and example scripts before closure.
serial.unfinished_or_incorrect: No serial coordination work was unfinished; the current official evaluation passed and the process completed normally with a substantive final response.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: The parallel run recognized and implemented the same required retry APIs, packaging, testing, examples, and instrumentation scope.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: The serial run recognized the same requirements and used them to guide a direct end-to-end implementation and final report.
comparison_dimensions.difference: No material requirement-recognition difference explains the official outcome; both artifacts passed the current official evaluation.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: The parent owned implementation and later decomposed verification into a six-child workflow for packaging, import surface, snippets, behavior, robustness, and verifier work.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: The serial run had no delegation; one actor owned implementation, docs, examples, tests, cleanup, and closure.
comparison_dimensions.difference: The main difference is late verification fan-out in parallel, not a different implementation owner; serial avoided child lifecycle risk by completing checks directly.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: The verification children received a detailed read-only audit context with spec, target source, upstream reference, environment, and hard rules.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: The serial actor carried context locally and did not need child handoffs or cross-agent interface contracts.
comparison_dimensions.difference: No missing brief or cross-agent implementation interface explains behavior; the adverse event was lifecycle termination after a reasonably detailed audit brief.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: The parallel parent wrote the source package, configuration, tests, and metadata itself, leaning on upstream behavior and local checks before the late workflow.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: The serial actor similarly wrote source, configuration, tests, examples, and docs directly, using upstream sdists as behavioral references.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Both implementation paths produced passing Stamina packages; serial delivered a fuller examples/docs tree while parallel's artifact had only one example listed at official artifact capture.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: The late verification workflow was launched, partial child results appeared, and then the workflow state recorded killed/aborted with several children still active.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: The serial actor retained direct control of results and ended with a normal final response summarizing deliverables and verification.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel had a concrete child-result lifecycle failure; serial had no child join boundary and completed result presentation.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Implementation writes were centralized in the parent; children were instructed not to modify /workspace, and no concrete concurrent overwrite is evidenced.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: The serial actor wrote and cleaned a coherent final tree with docs, examples, source, tests, and metadata.
comparison_dimensions.difference: No shared-state collision differentiates the passing outcomes; the visible artifact difference is that serial retained more docs/examples in the final tree.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: The parent ran local tests, upstream tests, clean install checks, and then launched additional adversarial verification that did not finish.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: The serial actor ran own tests, upstream tests, combined tests, wheel/install checks, compile checks, and examples, then reported those results.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Both had enough verification for official pass; parallel lost the added verifier workflow, while serial completed verification and described it at closure.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: The parallel process consumed the full budget, ended with returncode 143, and had an empty final response despite a passing artifact.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: The serial process completed normally with returncode 0 and remaining budget, then wrote a substantive final response.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Budget pressure and timeout harmed parallel closure but not the official pass; serial closed cleanly without delegation overhead.

outcome_analysis.explanation: The current completed official evaluations show both the parallel and serial artifacts passed. The concrete task-solving difference is therefore process and closure quality rather than pass/fail: serial completed its single-actor verification and final report, while parallel launched a late verification workflow that was killed and left the response empty.
ordinary_implementation_differences: The serial final artifact list includes docs and five examples, while the parallel official artifact list includes one example and no docs.
The parallel final response is empty because the process timed out; the serial final response describes the completed package and verification.

candidates.reason: The parent directly owned and wrote the implementation modules before delegation; there was an implementation owner.
The parent integrated the package source and no separately owned component implementations required reconciliation.
The parent assembled the installable workspace and the official artifact passed; missing final text is closure, not assembly ownership.
The parent owned the end-to-end implementation, testing, package verification, and workflow launch pipeline.
Implementation was not blocked behind a mandatory serial preflight; the parent began writing source early and verified later.
The parallel run did not defer productive implementation until after a separate investigation phase; implementation preceded the late workflow.
No indispensable implementation or integration path was starved; the passed package was already built before the verification workflow failed.

The six-child workflow and timeout are visible, but the direct qualifying boundary is explicit workflow abortion of active children rather than proven excessive breadth displacing indispensable task work.
No single child is proven to have an overbroad assignment whose scope uniquely caused unfinished indispensable work; several children were simply interrupted.

The workflow brief included the implementation under audit, spec file, upstream reference, environment, read-only rule, and expected verification behavior; no omitted known requirement caused unusable child work.
The children were read-only verifiers rather than producers of separately owned interoperating implementation components.
No known finding or requirement is shown present before transfer and missing after transfer; unfinished handoffs were due to termination.
No completed returned handoff is shown to be too large or insufficiently structured for the parent to consume within a decision window.
No receiver consumed a superseded workspace, dependency, or requirement state; the workflow was interrupted before aggregate consumption.
No incompatible completed child reports are shown reaching the parent and remaining unadjudicated at a decision point.
The parent did not make a final whole-task completion decision after the workflow; instead the process timed out and the official evaluator later passed the artifact.
There is no replacement or retry child assigned the same scope without inherited findings or checkpointed workspace state.

taxonomy_decisions.sub_label: Wrong Start, Join, or Result Timing

candidates.reason: The parent launched an executed verification workflow, and the workflow state records it killed with active children still in progress before the needed aggregate verifier result finalized.
candidates.realized_consequence: The added adversarial verification work produced no aggregate return, several audit/verifier children remained unfinished, and the parent timed out with an empty final response.
candidates.near_match_reason: The closest result-timing alternative is not as direct because no finalized verifier finding is shown trapped below the parent; the children were stopped before verifier work finalized.

candidates.reason: There was no complete unpromoted workflow result or compatible child component set waiting for placement; the active workflow work was interrupted before completion.
No child implementation change was integrated after relevant whole-package verification without a follow-up check; the children were read-only verifiers.
No delegated implementation was completed and left unretrieved; implementation was parent-owned and the delegated workflow was verification-only.
The workflow did not contain a finalized concrete verifier finding trapped below the parent; the stronger direct event is cancellation of still-running verifier and audit children.
The run ended at the same cancellation/timeout boundary, so there was no separately observable parent decision point after a child failure where takeover was omitted.
The parent inspected workflow progress and completed audit snippets; there is no complete aggregate child result that was visible and ignored.
The parent did not simply wait blindly; it checked workflow progress and ran other verification before the timeout.
No live agents wrote competing implementation files or overlapping behavior designs; child workflow instructions prohibited /workspace modification.
There is no evidence that two live actors edited the same source or configuration file and had to reconcile concurrent changes.
No actor replaced or wholesale rewrote non-entry source that another active actor owned.
No build, copy, install, edit, or child action replaced a submitted deliverable while another actor owned or used it.
No broad cleanup, rebuild, or promotion invalidated another agent's final-tree work or provenance.
Although children shared the workspace for reading, no concrete unstable-state or provenance problem from live shared writes is shown.
No generated artifact, cache, temp file, process, or auxiliary implementation from one concurrent actor was consumed by another as stable reference input.
